question.text: Which of the following is identified as one of SEBI's functions in relation to industry bodies in the securities market?

answer.text: Replacing all industry associations with government-run regulators
Promoting and regulating self-regulatory organizations (SROs) in the securities market
Auditing the financial statements of every listed company directly
Setting interest rates for the banking sector

explanation.text: The Logic: The NISM Series XV workbook lists, among SEBI's functions, the role of promoting and regulating self-regulatory organizations (SROs) in the securities market. SROs are industry bodies recognized to set and enforce certain standards on their members under SEBI's overall oversight. The Trap: SEBI does not replace industry associations with government regulators, does not directly audit individual listed companies' financials, and does not set banking interest rates (that role belongs to the central bank). Note: The NISM Series XV (Research Analyst) workbook supports the function of "promoting and regulating self-regulatory organizations in the securities market" as one of SEBI's functions, but the more elaborate definition of SROs as "industry associations regulating their own members under SEBI oversight" — and the example of AMFI — was not located in the workbook pages reviewed. The framing above is presented as the directly source-supported statement of the rule.
